newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine poultry firms cut output to survive.
newsitem.headline: Philippine poultry firms cut output to survive.

text.p: Philippine poultry firms had agreed to cut output by an average of 30 percent each to survive the glut that has put the industry under a cloud, an industry official said on Monday.
Swift, a unit of RFM Corp, had cut its chicken production by 10 percent, RFM Corp executive vice-president Felicisimo Nacino Jr said.
He said Swift had agreed with five other companies to cut chicken production this year.

The other firms which had agreed to the production cut were San Miguel Corp, Pure Foods Corp, Vitarich Corp, Universal Robina Corp and unlisted General Milling Corp, Nacino told Reporters at a news conference organised by brokerage Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Sun Hung Kai was recommending RFM as one of the stocks to buy among mid-sized companies.
Officials of the other food companies were not immediately available to confirm the production cut agreement.
"We've cut back production to survive and already we feel the start of the turnaround for the first two months of the year," Nacino said.
Last month, Swift reported a net loss of 200.723 million pesos in the first half ended December. The losses were mainly because of higher costs of corn and excessive supplies in the market.
Nacino said the price of dressed chicken now at 52 pesos is expected to rise to 56 pesos by the end of the month.
